OPTIONS

Ball cam locks onto the ball with a level horizon. Turn it off to orbit with middle-mouse drag or the controller right stick. Field of view is horizontal; distance and height are in centimetres.

KEYBOARD / MOUSE BINDINGS

Select a binding, then press a key or mouse button. Escape pauses; Enter skips a replay.

CONTROLLER BINDINGS

Xbox and PlayStation controllers use the browser’s standard mapping. Reassigning an occupied button swaps the two actions. Menus use A / Cross to select and B / Circle to go back.

HOW TO PLAY

YOUR FIRST AERIAL Hold jump, tilt the nose up, then boost. Use air roll to land wheels down. Resting upside down? Press Jump to flip back onto your wheels. Change your bindings in Options → Controls.

Controller: RT/LT drive, left stick steer/pitch, A jump, B boost, X powerslide, Y ball cam, LB/RB air roll, Start pause. Free camera: turn ball cam off, then drag the middle mouse button or use the right stick to look around. Play with a keyboard or gamepad.

ABOUT BOOST CIRCUIT

Boost Circuit is an independent car-soccer recreation inspired by Rocket League. It uses original game code, your supplied Champions Field stadium and Fennec model with procedural wheel animation, and Three.js rendering on your device.

Arena measurements, boost behavior and jump references come from RLGym and the RLBot community. Psyonix’s gameplay guides informed the camera, training and match flow. Source values and unit conversions are audited; contact response, wall adhesion and bot skill remain approximations.

Play local bot matches, free play, training, automatic online 1v1 or private matches with one friend. Online Match searches for 60 seconds before starting a bot match. NetplayJS’s shared connection service introduces the two browsers; one player hosts the simulation. Rocket League accounts and native physics parity are not included.

Fennec model by Jako, supplied by you and adapted under CC BY 4.0. Wheel pivots, materials and browser optimization have been added.

Champions Field stadium by Prabhu Ram / virtualmakes, adapted from your supplied model under CC BY 4.0. Architecture and banners are retained; materials are adapted and the inner pitch uses calibrated game surfaces. Original stadium model ↗

Physics references: RocketSim, rl_ball_sym and RocketGPU. Bot strategy references: RLBot-Beast. Values cross-checked with rl.source.gs. Reference licenses.

Interface references: Game UI Database (requested reference; access blocked during this update) and Interface In Game (screenshots reviewed). Menus and HUD are recreated in HTML, CSS and SVG. Rajdhani by Indian Type Foundry is used under the SIL Open Font License.

Networking references: NetplayJS (ISC; signaling protocol and authoritative synchronization) and Multicore (planning and version-compatibility reference). NetplayJS license.

Bottled car by Urizel, supplied by you under CC BY-NC 4.0. Adapted scale, wheel rig and glass; texture encoding optimized. Original model ↗.

Octane model by Jako, supplied by you and adapted under CC BY 4.0. Original model ↗.

cHe by luyssport, adapted under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Its adapted model and garage illustration retain that license. Original model ↗.

Cyberpunk bike by daCruz, based on Fernando Correa’s concept, adapted under CC BY-NC 4.0. Original model ↗.

Boeing C-17B Globemaster III by Muhamad Mirza Arrafi, adapted under CC BY 4.0. Original model ↗.

These supplied models have adapted scale, wheel rigs and textures. The bike and plane are novelty bodies with the same handling as the cars. Rocket League ball artwork was supplied by you; creator and license details were not included in its archive.

Additional supplied novelty models: Randy Marsh, Ridiculous Vehicle and Viking wagon (author/license notices were not supplied); sci-fi vehicle by 3DHaupt, golf cart by bcwilcox and IFV by adilwork23 (CC BY 4.0); autorickshaw by gourav.das3650 (Sketchfab Standard). All retain their source artwork, use the shared game hitbox, and have adapted animation rigs.
